mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays flat or slightly positive while WORKPLACES, TRANSIT, and RETAIL_REC all fall together, people are spending more time near home and making fewer discretionary trips, which pushes retail-and-recreation mobility lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains near zero or positive but RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week average within 28 days, the mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A further one-week decline in TRANSIT below its current level indicates weakening interzonal movement and commute-linked foot traffic; that loss transmits to retail and recreation within one to two weeks through fewer incidental trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -17 points and stays there for 1 week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT drops below -17 and RETAIL_REC does not fall further within the next 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM turns negative while PARKS also deepens, households are shifting away from routine out-of-home errands and leisure trips; that combination should drag RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as discretionary visit frequency weakens.
failure_condition: If both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS are below their current weekly means for two straight weeks but RETAIL_REC does not remain below its last-4-week average over the following month, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A continued decline in WORKPLACES below -22 signals fewer in-person work trips; that reduces lunchtime and after-work shopping traffic, making RETAIL_REC weaker within the next one to four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -22 and remains there for 2 weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stays below -22 for two weeks but RETAIL_REC does not decline relative to the previous four weeks within 28 days, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS remains sharply below baseline, warm-weather leisure demand is not offsetting indoor retail trips; the same outdoor-demand slowdown should keep RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks rather than rebound.
failure_condition: If PARKS stays materially negative but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior-4-week mean within 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A synchronized drop in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES is a short-lag signal of stricter movement limits or voluntary avoidance; when both weaken together, retail and recreation should fall further over the next one to two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall week-on-week
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both decline week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not decline within 7 to 14 days, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As GROCERY_PHARM turns negative while RESIDENTIAL stays near zero, errands are consolidating into fewer trips and more at-home time; that pattern should suppress discretionary retail visits and keep RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls below 0 while RESIDENTIAL stays within ±1 point for 2 weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM is negative for two weeks and RESIDENTIAL remains near baseline but RETAIL_REC does not fall below its prior-4-week average by week 4, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Because RETAIL_REC has already fallen more steeply than TRANSIT and WORKPLACES over the last month, the current downward momentum should carry forward for at least one more month unless the labor-mobility series reverse first.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT or WORKPLACES rebound materially while RETAIL_REC still rises, the momentum-based decline hypothesis is rejected.
